title: Xenon tetrafluoride in three dimensions
hook: Turn a model of XeF₄ and examine its shape.

knows: Atoms or cells can be represented with simplified models.
doesNotKnow: Six electron regions surround xenon. Two are lone pairs opposite one another, leaving four fluorine atoms in a square plane.

misconception: A familiar diagram automatically reveals the structure or function.
objective: Six electron regions surround xenon. Two are lone pairs opposite one another, leaving four fluorine atoms in a square plane.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: Six electron regions surround xenon. Two are lone pairs opposite one another, leaving four fluorine atoms in a square plane.
The stage is a schematic model and is not drawn to scale.
claims.source: Explicit modelling convention in the stage and reveal.

recall.question: What is the molecular shape of XeF₄ around its central atom?
